items.headline: Dollar holds its CPI gains in Asia — DXY ~102.22, near a two-week high; EUR/USD ~$1.1168, GBP/USD ~$1.3345, USD/JPY ~158.72, AUD/USD ~$0.6870, NZD/USD ~$0.5605 (Reuters Asia wrap, Nov 11).
items.source: FXStreet Nov 11 — https://www.fxstreet.com/news/united-states-dollar-index-steadies-on-fed-rate-hike-odds-202611110347 ; Reuters Asia wrap via https://cruisin929.com/2026/11/10/dollar-gains-traction-as-fed-speakers-warn-of-risks-from-inflation/

items.headline: Dec Fed hike fully priced — CME FedWatch 25bp 91.9% (up from 84% a day earlier), 50bp 9.1%, pause priced out; better-than-even odds of a second hike in Jan. Waller set the 50bp trigger (core ≥0.3%); Paulson: CPI “shows that inflationary pressures remain clearly evident”; Logan: “at least two more rate increases, each by 25bp”.
items.source: Reuters Nov 11 (see item above) ; Stocktwits Nov 11 — https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/markets-are-bracing-for-another-fed-rate-hike-in-december-but-could-it-be-twice-as-big-as-expected/cNGDebvR9JS

items.headline: Brent $92.54 / WTI $86.68 (OilPriceAPI 03:56Z) — Brent above the $92.50 trigger as Hormuz shipping attacks keep the bid; 37 ships hit in Oct (highest monthly total since the war began), 10 so far in Nov; LSEG: even a deal would not restore flows without mine clearance, insurance and willing shippers.

Qatar says it secured two weeks to push US–Iran talks and hold off a new strike (JPost, citing diplomatic sources) — major gaps remain on the blockade timeline, nuclear issues and unfreezing funds; no US confirmation, and Tehran still denies any talks are happening.
items.source: Jerusalem Post via Lookonchain Nov 10 — https://lookonchain.com/feeds/81547 (URL from breaking-watch item)

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine-US talks open in Abu Dhabi — first three-way meeting since February; US envoy Kushner says recent contacts had “created real momentum”; Russia struck 10 Ukrainian regions and five substations overnight even as talks opened; Lavrov: no immediate ceasefire without knowing what happens next.
Gold steadies ~$4,039 in Asia after Tuesday’s -2.6% slide (~$4,032); 10Y ~4.98%, 2Y ~4.73% (Tue late-session closes); US bond market closed Wed for Veterans Day — no US data today.
items.source: Kitco Nov 10 — https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-11-10/gold-silver-retreat-high-core-cpi-lifts-december-fed-hike-odds-kitco-am ; Reuters Nov 11 (see first item)

items.headline: Dollar holds its CPI gains into the NY close — DXY ~102.2 (+0.51%), still below Fri’s 102.33 close; EUR/USD ~1.1166, GBP/USD ~1.3325 (-0.86%), USD/JPY ~158.79, AUD/USD ~0.6855 (-1.0%, weakest major), USD/CAD ~1.4195, NZD/USD ~0.5597 (Reuters, investingLive, breaking-watch Finnhub read).

Dec Fed hike effectively certain after the hot CPI — CME FedWatch afternoon reads split ~85% for 25bp / ~15% for 50bp (InvestingLive ~12% for 50bp; FXStreet had ~99% for 25bp at 14:15Z); Reuters poll: all 101 economists expect +25bp Dec 9. 2Y 4.76% (+21bp), 10Y back above 5.00%.

$42B 10Y auction soft — high yield 5.020%, BTC 2.46 (below the 2.60 six-auction avg), indirects 61.2% (vs 80.3% in Oct) — weak foreign demand; dealers take 9.8%. Second soft refunding sale in two days after the 3Y tailed 0.5bp Mon.
items.source: US Treasury 10Y auction results, Nov 10 (figures in calendar us-10y-auction-20261110)

items.headline: BoC Summary of Deliberations: council debated hold vs hike on Oct 28 and chose 2.50%; energy “higher for longer” with cost pass-through building; CPI seen 3.5% end-2026, above 3% through much of 2027, back to 2% mid-2028; growth revised up. Dec further-hike ~32-36%, hold the base case.
items.source: Bank of Canada Summary of Deliberations, Nov 10 (figures in calendar cad-boc-minutes-20261110)

items.headline: Oil recovers off the sub-$90 morning low — Brent ~$91.99, WTI ~$86.41 into the close as the Iran premium keeps unwinding (Brent -5.85% Mon to a $92.57 settle); gold slides ~2.8% to ~$4,023 as yields jump. API weekly crude stocks due 4:30pm CT.

Oct CPI HOT — headline +0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% fcst, prev +0.6%), core +0.3% (vs +0.2%, prev +0.3%) — core hits Waller's 50bp trigger exactly; no y/y published (Oct 2025 data gap). Dec hike fully priced; the question is now 25bp vs 50bp
Dollar jumps on the hot CPI — DXY ~101.9 (+0.36%, Investing.com ~08:37 ET); USD strongest vs AUD (+0.72%), least vs CAD (+0.30%); EUR/USD 1.1184, GBP/USD 1.3395, USD/JPY 158.40

Waller turns CPI into a 25bp-vs-50bp test: +25bp in Dec even if Oct CPI cools; 50bp if core prints ~0.3% or higher — 'hiking only 25bp would put our credibility at risk'. Dec hike now fully priced (~95.6-99% CME FedWatch), up from ~82% Mon; 2Y +6bp to ~4.61%
Brent falls below $90 for the first time since Aug ($89.92-90.2, -2.5-2.9%) as Trump says the Iran war is 'effectively over' and holds off new strikes; WTI ~$84.6-84.7 (-2.4-2.6%)
Dollar steadies into Oct CPI (7:30am CT, fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y — BLS publishes no annual rate); DXY ~101.7, EUR/USD ~1.1220, GBP/USD ~1.3425, USD/JPY ~158.1 after Waller's lift
Gold slips below $4,100 (~$4,097) as Waller's hawkish turn firms the dollar; silver ~$53.27
BoE's Lombardelli 'wouldn't rule out' a December rate hike (Guardian); sterling gives back its 1.3459 London high to ~1.3425 on Waller's dollar lift

BoJ Summary of Opinions turns hawkish: several members want faster hikes toward neutral, 'without becoming overly cautious'; one sees neutral 'considerably above 1%' — Dec hike to 1.50% stays ~80% priced; USD/JPY ~157.98
China Oct trade: surplus $105.3B misses ($126.5B fcst) as imports surge +41.6% y/y (vs +32% exp); exports +35.2% beat — cumulative surplus tops $1T for a second straight year; no FX leg (AUD ~$0.692)
NY Fed Oct survey: inflation expectations flat at 3.9% (1y) / 3.3% (3y) / 3.0% (5y) — still above target; jobless-rate expectations hit the highest since April 2020
Dollar gives back Friday's payrolls jump at the NY close — DXY ~101.84 (-0.48%), EUR/USD ~1.1204, GBP/USD ~1.3415, USD/JPY ~158.01; NZD +1.56% to $0.5616 leads as risk rebounds

Bailey in Zurich: AI an early positive supply shock for the UK (nearly a fifth of GDP growth since early 2026); warns of an 'AI asset price bubble'; stresses central-bank independence — no new December steer
